title: Hypocalcemia: presentation and bedside signs
sec: Hypocalcemia: presentation and bedside signs · p883
guide: Distinguish acute excitability, long QT and seizures from chronic calcification, cataract and dry skin. Elicit latent tetany with facial tapping or cuff inflation; the two tests are not interchangeable. ECG intervals require rate correction in clinical use.

title: Hypocalcemia: phosphate–PTH cause branches
guide: Use phosphate and PTH together: low PTH suggests deficient secretion; normal/high PTH directs attention to renal failure, cell injury and other causes. DiGeorge: TBX1/22q11.2 and CATCH22; adult autoimmune disease: APECED.

title: Drug causes, hungry bone and PTH resistance
sec: Drug causes, hungry bone and PTH resistance · p885
guide: Confirm corrected/ionized calcium, assess magnesium, then evaluate PTH. Compare hungry bone with gland failure. Read PHP types across biochemical resistance, cAMP response and AHO, while recognizing the printed PPHP response wording is misleading.

title: AHO, knuckle patterns and calcium treatment
sec: AHO, knuckle patterns and calcium treatment · p886
guide: AHO combines brachydactyly, short stature, round facies and cognitive impairment. Separate 3rd-, 4th-, and 4th/5th-knuckle patterns. Source calcium regimens are learning references, not unmonitored prescribing instructions.
